title: NEC Past Paper - Set 19 (2083 Asoj 19, 2nd shift)

questions.stem: The moment of inertia of a hollow rectangular section of outer breadth B and depth D with an inner rectangle b × d, about the centroidal axis, is:
questions.solution: **(BD³ − bd³)/12.** Both rectangles share the same centroidal axis, so the inner one is simply subtracted from the outer.

examTip.trap: Dividing by 3 is the value about the *base*, and the hollow section is almost always asked about the centroid.
examTip.trick: Subtract, because the material is missing — and keep the /12 of the centroidal axis.

questions.stem: The standard size of a brick as per the Nepal Building Code is:
questions.solution: **240 × 115 × 57 mm.** 240 × 115 × 57 mm is the nominal brick; adding a 10 mm mortar joint gives the modular size of 250 × 125 × 67 mm.

examTip.trap: 250 × 125 × 67 mm is the *modular* size including the joint, which is the number that looks rounder and more memorable.
examTip.trick: The brick itself is smaller than the module it occupies in the wall.

questions.stem: Which masonry requires the highest level of skill for laying?
questions.solution: **Dry rubble masonry.** With no mortar at all, every stone must be shaped and seated so the wall stands by interlock alone — the most demanding work on site.

examTip.trap: Ashlar needs the finest *dressing*, but the stones are regular and the laying is straightforward once they are cut.
examTip.trick: No mortar means no tolerance for error.
examTip.mnemonic: Dry rubble: no mortar, no margin.

questions.stem: For a well-graded soil, the coefficient of curvature Cc lies between:
questions.solution: **1 and 3.** A well-graded soil needs Cc between 1 and 3 together with Cu greater than 4 for gravel or 6 for sand.

examTip.trap: The numbers 4 and 6 belong to the uniformity coefficient Cu, and the two criteria are routinely mixed up.
examTip.trick: Cc is the shape of the curve (1-3); Cu is its spread (>4 or >6).

questions.stem: Which grading zone of fine aggregate is the coarsest as per IS 383?
questions.solution: **Zone I.** The zones run from coarsest to finest, so Zone I is the coarsest sand and Zone IV the finest.

examTip.trap: Zone II is the one most used in concrete, so it is the zone that comes to mind first.
examTip.trick: The number rises as the sand gets finer.
examTip.mnemonic: Zone I coarse, Zone IV fine.

questions.stem: The falling head permeability test is suitable for:
questions.solution: **Fine-grained soils of low permeability.** In a soil of low permeability the flow is too small to measure by constant head, so the fall of water in a standpipe is observed instead.

examTip.trap: The constant head test is the one for coarse soils, and the two are paired in every textbook.
examTip.trick: Low flow needs a falling head; high flow needs a constant head.

questions.stem: A quick sand condition occurs when the:
questions.solution: **Effective stress becomes zero.** Upward seepage raises the pore pressure until it equals the total stress, leaving no effective stress and therefore no shear strength.

examTip.trap: "Quick sand" sounds like a property of the sand; it is a hydraulic condition that can occur in any cohesionless soil.
examTip.trick: σ′ = σ − u, and quick sand is σ′ = 0.

questions.stem: Consolidation settlement of a clay occurs because of:
options: Expulsion of water from the voids
questions.solution: **Expulsion of water from the voids.** Both the water and the mineral grains are effectively incompressible; the volume change comes entirely from water being squeezed out.

examTip.trap: "Compression" in the name suggests the material is being compressed, when it is the void space that closes.
examTip.trick: Consolidation takes time precisely because water has to travel out.

questions.stem: An element carries a normal stress σx and a shear stress τxy. The maximum shear stress is:
questions.solution: **√((σx/2)² + τxy²).** The maximum shear stress is the radius of Mohr's circle, built on σx/2 and τxy as the two sides of a right triangle.

examTip.trap: Adding the two stresses directly ignores that they act on perpendicular planes.
examTip.trick: The radius of the circle is always a root of two squares.

questions.stem: In a kerb length of 59 m, how many vehicles 5 m long can be parked parallel to the kerb?
questions.solution: **9.** Parallel parking needs 5.9 m per car including the manoeuvring gap, so 59/5.9 = 10 bays — but the first bay needs no gap, giving 9 in the usual N = (L − 1.25)/5.9 form.

examTip.trap: Dividing 59 by 5 gives a tidy 11 or 12 and ignores the gap every car needs to get in and out.
examTip.trick: Parallel parking always needs more than the vehicle length per bay.

questions.stem: Active earth pressure develops on a retaining wall when the wall:
questions.solution: **Moves away from the backfill.** Yielding away lets the soil expand laterally and mobilise its shear strength, which reduces the pressure to its active minimum.

examTip.trap: Movement towards the fill produces *passive* pressure, which is much larger — the two cases are mirror images.
examTip.trick: Away from the soil: active and small. Into the soil: passive and large.

questions.stem: Which drain runs full only during the rainy season?
questions.solution: **An open surface drain.** Open surface drains carry storm water only, so they are dry for most of the year and full during the monsoon.

examTip.trap: A combined sewer also swells in the monsoon, but it carries sewage all year and is never empty.
examTip.trick: Only a storm-water-only drain can be dry in the dry season.

questions.stem: The minimum depth of a footing below ground level is generally:
questions.solution: **500 mm.** A minimum of 500 mm takes the base below the zone affected by seasonal moisture change, erosion and surface disturbance.

examTip.trap: 1000 mm and above are the depths adopted in expansive black cotton soils, which makes them look like the safer general figure.
examTip.trick: The general minimum is half a metre; particular soils demand more.

questions.stem: The position of the groundwater table is observed by means of:
questions.solution: **An observation well.** A perforated pipe is left in the ground and the water level inside it is read once it has come to equilibrium with the aquifer.

examTip.trap: The other three instruments measure flow, rainfall and humidity — all water-related and none of them a water level.
examTip.trick: To read a level, you need something the water can stand in.

questions.stem: An ideal fluid is one that is:
options: Of constant viscosity at all temperatures
questions.solution: **Incompressible and has zero viscosity.** An ideal fluid has no viscosity, so it offers no resistance to shear and loses no energy to friction, and its density does not change.

examTip.trap: A fluid obeying Newton's law of viscosity is a *Newtonian* fluid, which is a different idealisation and definitely has viscosity.
examTip.trick: Ideal means frictionless; Newtonian means linearly viscous.

questions.stem: Absolute pressure is related to gauge pressure by:
questions.solution: **Pabs = Pgauge + Patm.** Gauge pressure is measured from atmospheric, so adding atmospheric pressure brings it back to the absolute zero datum.

examTip.trap: Subtracting is correct for *vacuum* pressure, which is measured downwards from atmospheric.
examTip.trick: Absolute is always the larger of the two for a pressurised fluid.
examTip.mnemonic: Add the atmosphere to get absolute.

questions.stem: The expression fLV²/(2gd) for head loss in a pipe is due to:
questions.solution: **Darcy-Weisbach.** The Darcy-Weisbach equation gives the friction head loss in terms of a dimensionless friction factor f.

examTip.trap: Hazen-Williams is the other common pipe friction formula, but it is empirical and uses a C value with fractional powers.
examTip.trick: A dimensionless f with V² and L/d is Darcy-Weisbach.

questions.stem: When the depth of flow in a channel is less than the critical depth, the slope is:
questions.solution: **Steep.** Flow shallower than critical is supercritical, which a steep slope produces: on a steep slope the normal depth is below the critical depth.

examTip.trap: A mild slope gives a normal depth *above* critical, which is the subcritical case.
examTip.trick: Steep slope, fast shallow flow; mild slope, slow deep flow.

questions.stem: The deflection at the centre of a fixed beam carrying a central point load W is:
questions.solution: **WL³/192EI.** Fixing both ends reduces the simply supported deflection WL³/48EI by a factor of four.

examTip.trap: WL³/384EI is the uniformly distributed case on a fixed beam, so the two fixed-beam results are easily swapped.
examTip.trick: Point load: 48 simple, 192 fixed. UDL: 5/384 simple, 1/384 fixed.

questions.stem: The deflection at the free end of a cantilever carrying a point load W at that end is:
questions.solution: **WL³/3EI.** The largest of the standard deflections, because the cantilever has no support at the loaded end.

examTip.trap: WL³/8EI is the cantilever with a uniformly distributed load, differing only in the denominator.
examTip.trick: Cantilever point load 3, cantilever UDL 8.

questions.stem: When the load factor and the diversity factor of a power system both increase, the cost of electricity:
questions.solution: **Decreases.** Both factors mean the installed plant is used more evenly, so the same capital serves more units and the cost per unit falls.

examTip.trap: Higher factors sound like heavier loading and therefore higher cost; they actually mean better utilisation.
examTip.trick: Better utilisation always spreads the fixed cost further.

questions.stem: In rate analysis, the cost of office establishment (overheads) is usually taken as:
questions.solution: **4%.** Office or establishment charges are about 4% of the work cost; contractor's profit is a separate 10-15%.

examTip.trap: 10-15% is the contractor's profit and is the better-known percentage in any estimate.
examTip.trick: Establishment is a small overhead, well below the profit margin.

questions.stem: For a single point load moving across a simply supported beam, the shear force at a given section is a maximum when the load is:
options: Just to one side of that section
questions.solution: **Just to one side of that section.** The influence line for shear jumps by unity at the section, so the maximum ordinate is reached with the load immediately beside it.

examTip.trap: Mid-span is where the *bending moment* peaks for a central load, and that result is carried across.
examTip.trick: Shear influence lines have a discontinuity at the section; put the load at the jump.

questions.stem: PERT stands for:
questions.solution: **Programme Evaluation and Review Technique.** PERT is the probabilistic network technique using three time estimates; CPM is its deterministic counterpart.

examTip.trap: All four expansions use plausible project-management words, so the acronym must actually be known.
examTip.trick: PERT reviews a programme; CPM finds a critical path.

questions.stem: When a uniformly distributed load acts on a three-hinged parabolic arch, the bending moment at every section is:
questions.solution: **Zero.** A parabola is the funicular shape for a UDL, so the thrust line coincides with the axis and no bending is induced anywhere.

examTip.trap: "Shear force is zero" is offered alongside and is not true — only the bending moment vanishes.
examTip.trick: Match the arch shape to the load and the bending disappears.
examTip.mnemonic: Parabola plus UDL equals pure thrust.

questions.stem: Space is left at the top of a sewer pipe mainly to:
options: Reduce the cost of the pipe by using a smaller diameter than needed
Allow a person to enter and inspect the sewer from the inside
Increase the velocity of flow by narrowing the cross-section of flow
Allow for peak and future flows and let foul gases escape
questions.solution: **Allow for peak and future flows and let foul gases escape.** Sewers are designed to run about three-quarters full at peak, leaving a free space for ventilation and for flows above the estimate.

examTip.trap: Accumulating gas is exactly what the space prevents — the free board lets it move to a vent rather than build up.
examTip.trick: A sewer running full has no ventilation and no reserve.

questions.stem: The nominal clear cover for a slab under mild exposure as per IS 456 is:
questions.solution: **20 mm.** 20 mm for a slab in mild exposure; it rises to 30 mm for moderate exposure and more for severe.

examTip.trap: 25 mm is the cover for a *beam* and 40 mm for a column — the same table, the next row down.
examTip.trick: Cover rises as the member carries more and sits closer to the ground.

questions.stem: The flexural strength of concrete is related to its characteristic compressive strength by:
questions.solution: **fcr = 0.7√fck.** IS 456 gives the modulus of rupture as 0.7√fck N/mm², used in the deflection and crack-width checks.

examTip.trap: 5000√fck is the modulus of elasticity from the same clause — a stiffness, not a strength.
examTip.trick: 0.7 is a strength, 5000 is a stiffness.

questions.stem: A rigid plane frame is statically determinate when:
questions.solution: **3m + r = 3j.** Each rigid member carries three unknown internal forces and each joint supplies three equations, so the count is 3m + r = 3j.

examTip.trap: m + r = 2j is the test for a plane *truss*, where members carry axial force only.
examTip.trick: Truss members carry one force; frame members carry three.

questions.stem: For a beam carrying unequal loads at several points, the most convenient method of finding the deflection is:
questions.solution: **The moment area method.** The moment area theorems handle any M/EI diagram geometrically and avoid writing a separate equation for every span segment.

examTip.trap: Double integration is perfectly valid but needs a new expression and two constants for every change in loading.
examTip.trick: Many load points mean many segments, so a graphical method wins.

questions.stem: Harmful disease-causing bacteria are called:
questions.solution: **Pathogens.** Pathogens are the organisms that cause disease; most bacteria in water are harmless or useful.

examTip.trap: Aerobes and saprophytes are classified by how they obtain energy, which has nothing to do with whether they cause disease.
examTip.trick: Patho- means disease.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a water-borne disease?
questions.solution: **Measles.** Measles is a viral infection spread through the air by droplets; the other three are transmitted by contaminated water.

examTip.trap: All four are infectious diseases common in the same communities, so the route of transmission is the only distinction.
examTip.trick: Ask how it gets into the body — by drinking or by breathing.

questions.stem: In conventional water treatment, the step immediately after coagulation is:
questions.solution: **Flocculation.** Coagulation destabilises the colloids by rapid mixing; gentle stirring then lets them collide and grow into settleable flocs.

examTip.trap: Filtration is the next *unit process* after sedimentation, which itself follows flocculation — so it is two steps too far.
examTip.trick: Coagulate, flocculate, sediment, filter, disinfect.
examTip.mnemonic: Coagulation makes it sticky, flocculation makes it big.

questions.stem: The self-cleansing (non-silting) velocity in a sewer is about:
questions.solution: **0.6 m/s.** About 0.6 m/s keeps organic solids in suspension; below that, deposits form and the sewer silts up.

examTip.trap: 3.0 m/s is the maximum non-scouring velocity at the other end of the range.
examTip.trick: 0.6 stops silting, 3.0 stops scouring.

questions.stem: The structure that separates the weir proper from the under-sluices is the:
questions.solution: **Divide wall.** A divide wall runs perpendicular to the weir axis and forms a still pocket in front of the head regulator, keeping the two flows apart.

examTip.trap: Guide bunds also separate flows, but they guide the river into the whole works rather than divide it internally.
examTip.trick: The wall divides the structure; the bund guides the river.

questions.stem: The function of a guide bund is to:
options: Raise the water level upstream so the canal can draw its full supply
Trap the bed load before it reaches the intake and enters the canal
Dissipate the energy of the flood flow as it passes over the structure
Confine the river to a defined width and lead it centrally through the works
questions.solution: **Confine the river to a defined width and lead it centrally through the works.** Guide bunds prevent the river outflanking the structure and keep the approach flow straight and central.

examTip.trap: A weir raises the water level; a guide bund does nothing to the level at all.
examTip.trick: Guiding is about direction, not about head.
examTip.mnemonic: Guide the flow, not the level.

questions.stem: Hydropower is classified as:
options: A renewable and conventional source of energy
questions.solution: **A renewable and conventional source of energy.** It is renewable because the hydrological cycle replenishes it, and conventional because it has been used at scale for over a century.

examTip.trap: "Renewable" and "non-conventional" are often treated as synonyms; solar and wind are both, but hydropower is renewable *and* conventional.
examTip.trick: Conventional is about how long it has been used, not about whether it runs out.

questions.stem: The process of laying and compacting earth in layers to build an embankment dam is called:
questions.solution: **Rolled fill construction.** Material is spread in thin layers and compacted by rollers to a specified density — the standard method for modern embankment dams.

examTip.trap: Hydraulic fill places the material as a slurry and lets it sort itself, which is the historic alternative.
examTip.trick: Rolling means mechanical compaction in layers.

questions.stem: The Registrar of the Nepal Engineering Council must be:
options: A civil servant of any background appointed by the responsible ministry
A member of parliament nominated by the house for a fixed term
A university professor of engineering nominated by the universities
A registered engineer with the prescribed qualification and experience
questions.solution: **A registered engineer with the prescribed qualification and experience.** The Act requires the Registrar to be an engineer registered with the Council and to hold the qualification and experience its regulations prescribe.

examTip.trap: The Registrar is an administrative head, which makes a general civil service background look sufficient.
examTip.trick: The Council regulates engineers, so its Registrar is one.

questions.stem: Fatigue cracking in a flexible pavement is caused by:
options: Tensile strain at the bottom of the bituminous layer
Compressive strain at the bottom of the bituminous layer
Compressive strain at the top of the subgrade
questions.solution: **Tensile strain at the bottom of the bituminous layer.** Each wheel pass bends the bound layer, putting its underside into tension; repeated cycles start a crack that works upwards.

examTip.trap: Compressive strain at the top of the subgrade is the *other* design criterion, and it governs rutting rather than cracking.
examTip.trick: Cracking needs tension, and the tension is underneath.

questions.stem: In a mass haul diagram, a positive (rising) ordinate indicates:
questions.solution: **Cut.** Cut is accumulated as positive and fill as negative, so a rising curve means earth is being excavated.

examTip.trap: Cut and fill are the only two options that matter, and the sign convention is the whole question.
examTip.trick: Rising means material is being gained from the ground.

questions.stem: A foundation is classed as shallow when:
questions.solution: **D/B ≤ 1.** Terzaghi's definition takes the depth as not greater than the width, so the shear strength of the soil above the base can be neglected.

examTip.trap: D/B ≥ 4 is the usual definition of a *deep* foundation, offered right beside it.
examTip.trick: Shallow means the depth is the smaller of the two.

questions.stem: The speed of the centrifuge in a bitumen extraction test is about:
questions.solution: **3000 rpm.** The bowl is spun at roughly 3000 revolutions per minute to throw the solvent and dissolved bitumen clear of the aggregate.

examTip.trap: All four options are plausible machine speeds, so the figure has to be remembered rather than reasoned.
examTip.trick: Three thousand is the standard laboratory centrifuge speed.

questions.stem: On the Moody diagram, the parameter e/d represents the:
questions.solution: **Relative roughness of the pipe.** e is the average height of the wall protrusions and d the diameter, so e/d is roughness expressed relative to the pipe size.

examTip.trap: The friction factor is what the diagram *gives*; e/d is one of the two inputs used to read it.
examTip.trick: Reynolds number on the bottom axis, relative roughness on the curves, friction factor on the side.
examTip.mnemonic: e over d is roughness, relative.

questions.stem: The Prithvi Highway connects:
questions.solution: **Kathmandu and Pokhara.** The Prithvi Highway runs from Naubise to Pokhara and is the main link between the capital and the western hills.

examTip.trap: Tribhuvan Highway goes to Birgunj, Siddhartha to Butwal and Araniko to Kodari — four highways, four destinations.
examTip.trick: Prithvi Narayan Shah's name is on the road towards Gorkha and Pokhara.

questions.stem: A nephelometer is used to measure:
questions.solution: **Turbidity.** It measures the intensity of light scattered at right angles to the beam, which is reported in nephelometric turbidity units.

examTip.trap: Colour is the neighbouring optical property and is measured by comparison on the platinum-cobalt scale.
examTip.trick: The unit NTU names the instrument.

questions.stem: Which part of the Nepal National Building Code deals with earthquake-resistant design of low-strength masonry buildings?
questions.solution: **NBC 203.** NBC 203 gives the mandatory guidelines for earthquake-resistant low-strength masonry buildings used for rural and non-engineered construction.

examTip.trap: NBC 105 is the seismic design code for *engineered* structures, and it is the one most often cited.
examTip.trick: 105 for engineered buildings, 201-203 for the mandatory rules of thumb.

questions.stem: A line drawn from the pole of Mohr's circle to a point on the circumference gives:
options: The magnitude of the principal stress
The direction of the plane on which those stresses act
questions.solution: **The direction of the plane on which those stresses act.** That is the defining property of the pole: any line from it to a point on the circle is parallel to the physical plane carrying that stress state.

examTip.trap: The stress magnitudes are read from the coordinates of the point; the pole gives the orientation instead.
examTip.trick: The pole converts the circle's geometry into real-world directions.
examTip.mnemonic: Pole gives planes, axes give stresses.

questions.stem: A simply supported beam under a uniformly distributed load is designed for:
options: Maximum bending moment at mid-span and maximum shear at the supports
Maximum bending moment and maximum shear both at mid-span
Maximum bending moment at the supports
questions.solution: **Maximum bending moment at mid-span and maximum shear at the supports.** The shear force is greatest at the supports where it equals the reaction, and zero at mid-span, where the bending moment peaks.

examTip.trap: Options putting both maxima at the same place are tempting because the mid-span moment is the famous one.
examTip.trick: Where shear is zero, moment is a maximum — they cannot peak together.
examTip.mnemonic: Moment in the middle, shear at the ends.

questions.stem: The axis of a gravity dam is the line of the crown of the dam on the:
questions.solution: **Upstream side.** The axis is the upstream edge of the crest and is the reference line for the whole layout of the dam.

examTip.trap: The centre of the base is the geometric middle and is the natural but wrong guess.
examTip.trick: The axis is set out at crest level, on the water side.

questions.stem: What distinguishes a profession from an occupation?
options: A higher salary than the one an ordinary occupation commands
Work carried out indoors rather than on a construction site
Specialised knowledge, formal training and a code of conduct
Compulsory membership of a trade union that negotiates on your behalf
questions.solution: **Specialised knowledge, formal training and a code of conduct.** A profession rests on a body of specialised knowledge, a required qualification, a duty to the public and self-regulation through a code of conduct.

examTip.trap: Receiving remuneration is common to both, so pay cannot be what separates them.
examTip.trick: Ask whether the public is owed a duty beyond the contract.

questions.stem: The purpose of pondage in a run-of-river hydropower scheme is to:
options: Store water from the wet season for use in the dry season
Raise the gross head of the plant
Store water for a few hours or days to meet peak demand
questions.solution: **Store water for a few hours or days to meet peak demand.** Pondage is short-term storage that lets the plant follow the daily demand curve; seasonal storage requires a reservoir.

examTip.trap: Seasonal storage is what a storage project such as Kulekhani provides, and the two words are easily confused.
examTip.trick: Pondage is hours and days; storage is months.
examTip.mnemonic: Pondage for the day, storage for the season.

questions.stem: The transportation of material on or by a fixed installation such as a belt or a chute is called:
questions.solution: **Conveying.** Conveying moves material continuously along a fixed path; hoisting lifts it vertically and hauling drags it horizontally by a moving vehicle.

examTip.trap: Hauling is also horizontal movement, but by a vehicle that travels with the load.
examTip.trick: The installation stays put and the material moves along it.

questions.stem: A free body diagram of a structural member shows:
options: All external forces and reactions acting on the isolated body
The bending moment and shear force diagrams
questions.solution: **All external forces and reactions acting on the isolated body.** The body is cut free of its surroundings and every external action on it, including reactions, is drawn in — that is what makes equilibrium applicable.

examTip.trap: BMD, SFD and axial force diagrams are *results* obtained after the free body is analysed.
examTip.trick: Free body means isolated, so everything the surroundings did must be replaced by a force.
examTip.mnemonic: Cut it free, draw every force.

questions.stem: The structure provided on a main canal just upstream of an off-taking canal is a:
questions.solution: **Cross regulator.** The cross regulator raises the water level in the main canal so that the off-take can draw its full supply even at low flow.

examTip.trap: The head regulator stands at the mouth of the off-take itself, on the branch rather than on the main canal.
examTip.trick: Cross regulator on the parent canal, head regulator on the branch.
examTip.mnemonic: Cross the main, head the branch.

questions.stem: The scour depth around a bridge pier is estimated using Lacey's formula, which is based on:
options: The silt factor of the bed material and the discharge
The suspended sediment load carried past the pier during the flood
The shape of the pier nose and the angle at which the flow meets it
The highest flood level recorded at the site over the design period
questions.solution: **The silt factor of the bed material and the discharge.** R = 0.47(Q/f)^(1/3), where f is the silt factor of the bed material — so the bed sediment and the discharge govern the regime scour depth.

examTip.trap: Suspended sediment is carried through and does not determine the regime depth, which is set by the bed material.
examTip.trick: The silt factor comes from the size of the particles on the bed.
examTip.mnemonic: Scour from bed material and Q.

questions.stem: Which distribution layout is used in an irregularly developed town with many cul-de-sacs?
questions.solution: **Dead end system.** The dead end (tree) system follows whatever street pattern exists and is the cheapest to lay, at the cost of stagnation at the ends.

examTip.trap: The grid iron system is the best hydraulically, but it requires a regularly planned street layout.
examTip.trick: Irregular streets force an irregular, branching network.

questions.stem: Which type of aggregate is NOT naturally found in Nepal?
questions.solution: **Basalt from marine volcanic deposits.** Nepal is landlocked and its geology is Himalayan sedimentary and metamorphic rock; marine volcanic basalt deposits do not occur.

examTip.trap: Basalt is a common concrete aggregate worldwide, which makes it sound like it should be available everywhere.
examTip.trick: Ask what Nepal's geology actually contains.

questions.stem: In chain surveying, the error caused by a chain that is too long is:
options: Measured lengths come out too short and must be increased
Measured lengths come out too long
questions.solution: **Measured lengths come out too short and must be increased.** A long chain spans more ground per chain length, so fewer chains are counted and the recorded distance is less than the true one.

examTip.trap: It feels as though a longer chain should give a longer reading; the reading is in chain *units*, so it gives fewer of them.
examTip.trick: True length = measured × (wrong length / correct length).
examTip.mnemonic: Chain too long, result too short.

questions.stem: The error that remains in a survey measurement after all known corrections have been applied, and that follows no fixed law, is:
questions.solution: **Accidental (random) error.** Accidental errors are as likely to be positive as negative and partly cancel; systematic errors accumulate and can be corrected.

examTip.trap: A mistake (blunder) is a gross error from carelessness and is not an error of measurement at all.
examTip.trick: If it can be corrected by a formula, it is systematic.

questions.stem: Bernoulli's equation is a statement of the conservation of:
questions.solution: **Energy along a streamline.** Pressure head, velocity head and datum head sum to a constant along a streamline for steady, incompressible, frictionless flow.

examTip.trap: The continuity equation expresses the conservation of mass and is applied alongside Bernoulli in almost every problem.
examTip.trick: Bernoulli adds heads, which are energies per unit weight.

questions.stem: A flow in which the velocity at a point does not change with time is called:
questions.solution: **Steady flow.** Steadiness concerns change with time; uniformity concerns change with position along the flow.

examTip.trap: Uniform flow is the companion definition and is the one that concerns space rather than time.
examTip.trick: Steady = ∂V/∂t = 0. Uniform = ∂V/∂s = 0.
examTip.mnemonic: Steady in time, uniform in space.

questions.stem: The net ultimate bearing capacity is obtained from the gross ultimate value by:
options: Dividing by the factor of safety
Subtracting the overburden pressure at founding level
questions.solution: **Subtracting the overburden pressure at founding level.** The soil already carried its own overburden before the footing was built, so only the net increase in pressure is new load.

examTip.trap: Dividing by the factor of safety gives the *safe* bearing capacity, which is the next step rather than this one.
examTip.trick: Net means the increase over what was there before.

questions.stem: The yield strength of Fe415 steel is:
questions.solution: **415 N/mm².** The number in the designation is the characteristic yield strength in newtons per square millimetre.

examTip.trap: 250 N/mm² is mild steel (Fe250) and 500 is the higher grade — all three are in common use.
examTip.trick: The grade number is the yield strength.

questions.stem: The camber provided on a bituminous road surface is normally about:
questions.solution: **2 to 2.5%.** Enough to drain the surface quickly without making the carriageway uncomfortable; earth roads need much more and cement concrete less.

examTip.trap: Earth and gravel roads take 3-4%, so the larger figures are right for a different surface.
examTip.trick: The smoother and less permeable the surface, the less camber it needs.

questions.stem: The passenger car unit (PCU) value of a bicycle is taken as:
questions.solution: **0.5.** A bicycle occupies about half the road space of a car in mixed traffic, so it is counted as 0.5 PCU.

examTip.trap: A car is the reference at 1.0 PCU, and that figure is the one everyone remembers.
examTip.trick: Smaller and slower vehicles take less road space, so less than one PCU.

questions.stem: In first-angle projection, the view obtained by looking from the left is placed on the:
questions.solution: **Right of the front view.** In first angle the object lies between the observer and the plane, so each view is pushed across to the far side of the front view.

examTip.trap: Third-angle projection puts the left view on the left, which is the arrangement that feels natural.
examTip.trick: First angle throws the view across; third angle keeps it on its own side.

questions.stem: Depreciation by the straight line method means the asset loses value:
options: By an equal percentage every year
Only at the end of its life
By an equal amount every year
questions.solution: **By an equal amount every year.** (Cost − scrap value)/life gives a fixed annual charge, so the book value falls along a straight line.

examTip.trap: An equal *percentage* each year is the declining balance method, which gives a curve rather than a line.
examTip.trick: Straight line means constant slope, which means a constant amount.

questions.stem: In CPM, the critical path is:
options: The shortest path through the network
The longest path through the network
The path with the most activities
The path with the highest cost
questions.solution: **The longest path through the network.** The project cannot finish before its longest chain of dependent activities is complete, so that chain determines the duration.

examTip.trap: "Critical" suggests urgency or importance, which makes the shortest or costliest path sound plausible.
examTip.trick: The project waits for its slowest chain.

questions.stem: The BOD of raw domestic sewage in Nepal is typically about:
questions.solution: **200-300 mg/l.** Medium-strength domestic sewage carries roughly 200-300 mg/l of five-day BOD; treated effluent must come down to about 20-30 mg/l.

examTip.trap: 20-30 mg/l is the standard for *treated* effluent and appears in the same tables.
examTip.trick: Raw sewage is about ten times the discharge standard.

questions.stem: Duty and delta are related by:
questions.solution: **Δ = 8.64B/D, with B in days.** Delta in metres equals 8.64 times the base period in days divided by the duty in hectares per cumec.

examTip.trap: Inverting B and D gives a formula that is dimensionally wrong and produces absurd depths.
examTip.trick: A higher duty irrigates more land per cumec, so the depth applied must be smaller — D belongs underneath.

questions.stem: A draft tube is used in a reaction turbine to:
options: Recover part of the kinetic energy leaving the runner
Increase the speed of the runner
Filter the water before the runner
questions.solution: **Recover part of the kinetic energy leaving the runner.** Its gradually increasing area converts the exit velocity head into pressure, allowing the turbine to be set above the tailrace without losing that head.

examTip.trap: An impulse turbine has no draft tube at all, because its runner discharges at atmospheric pressure.
examTip.trick: The draft tube recovers energy that would otherwise be thrown away.
examTip.mnemonic: Draft tube drafts the energy back.

questions.stem: A trench weir (Tyrolean intake) is especially suited to:
options: Wide rivers in the plains where the bed is flat and the flow is slow
Lakes and reservoirs where there is no current to carry sediment
Steep mountain streams carrying heavy bed load
Tidal estuaries where the direction of flow reverses twice a day
questions.solution: **Steep mountain streams carrying heavy bed load.** Water drops through a screen laid in the stream bed while boulders and gravel pass over the top, which suits a steep boulder-bearing torrent.

examTip.trap: A side intake is the usual arrangement on a large river, where a bed intake would silt at once.
examTip.trick: Bed intake for steep streams, side intake for wide rivers.

questions.stem: The seismic zone factor Z in NBC 105 represents:
options: The soil type at the site
The expected peak ground acceleration for the region
questions.solution: **The expected peak ground acceleration for the region.** Z scales the design force to the seismic hazard of the location, expressed as a fraction of gravity.

examTip.trap: Importance factor, soil factor and response reduction factor are the three other multipliers in the same expression.
examTip.trick: Z is about where the building is, not what it is.

questions.stem: In a doubly reinforced beam, compression steel is provided when:
options: The section cannot resist the moment as a singly reinforced section of that depth
The shear force at the support exceeds what the stirrups can carry
The span is short enough for the beam to behave as a deep beam
The cover to the tension steel is inadequate for the exposure condition
questions.solution: **The section cannot resist the moment as a singly reinforced section of that depth.** When the depth is restricted and the moment exceeds the limiting value, steel is added in the compression zone to make up the balance.

examTip.trap: High shear calls for stirrups, which is a different kind of reinforcement for a different action.
examTip.trick: Compression steel answers a moment problem, not a shear problem.

questions.stem: A retaining wall is checked against all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.solution: **Buckling of the stem.** The three stability checks are overturning, sliding and bearing; the stem is designed as a cantilever in bending, not for buckling.

examTip.trap: The stem is a vertical member, which makes buckling sound like a natural check — but it carries lateral pressure, not axial load.
examTip.trick: Buckling needs an axial compressive load, and the stem has almost none.

questions.stem: Prime coat is applied to:
options: An existing bituminous surface before an overlay
The wearing course as a final seal
A granular base, to bind and waterproof it before the bituminous layer
questions.solution: **A granular base, to bind and waterproof it before the bituminous layer.** A low-viscosity bitumen penetrates the porous granular base and plugs its surface voids so the layer above bonds properly.

examTip.trap: A *tack* coat is what goes on an existing bituminous surface, and the two coats are constantly confused.
examTip.trick: Prime the porous base, tack the bituminous one.

questions.stem: The contact time required for chlorine disinfection is about:
questions.solution: **30 minutes.** About half an hour of contact with a residual of 0.2 mg/l is needed for reliable disinfection before the water reaches the consumer.

examTip.trap: Shorter times are used in emergency dosing, and much longer ones in storage, so all the options are defensible in some context.
examTip.trick: The standard design contact period is half an hour.

questions.stem: The time of concentration of a catchment is the time taken for runoff to travel from:
options: The outlet to the watershed divide
The hydraulically most distant point to the outlet
The point of maximum rainfall to the outlet
The centroid of the catchment to the outlet
questions.solution: **The hydraulically most distant point to the outlet.** Once rain has lasted that long, the whole catchment is contributing to the outlet simultaneously and the peak discharge is reached.

examTip.trap: The centroid gives the *lag* time, a related but shorter interval used in unit hydrograph theory.
examTip.trick: The peak needs the farthest water to have arrived.

questions.stem: The section modulus Z of a rectangular section of breadth b and depth d is:
questions.solution: **bd²/6.** Z = I/ymax = (bd³/12)/(d/2) = bd²/6, and it carries the dimensions of length cubed.

examTip.trap: bd³/12 is the moment of inertia itself, one power of d larger.
examTip.trick: Divide the inertia by half the depth and one power of d disappears.
examTip.mnemonic: Section modulus Z = bd²/6; inertia I = bd³/12.

questions.stem: For a simply supported beam carrying a uniformly distributed load w over span L, the maximum bending moment is:
questions.solution: **wL²/8.** It occurs at mid-span where the shear force passes through zero.

examTip.trap: wL²/12 is the *fixed* beam support moment, and wL²/2 the cantilever moment — the same loading, different supports.
examTip.trick: Simple 1/8, fixed ends 1/12 and 1/24, cantilever 1/2.

questions.stem: In the centre line method of estimating, the length used is multiplied by:
options: The breadth and depth of each item of work
questions.solution: **The breadth and depth of each item of work.** The total centre line length is computed once and multiplied by the cross-section of each item, with a deduction at every junction.

examTip.trap: Forgetting the junction deduction is the classic error, and it is why the method is faster but less forgiving than long wall-short wall.
examTip.trick: One length, many cross-sections.

questions.stem: The main cause of waterlogging in an irrigated area is:
questions.solution: **Over-irrigation and inadequate drainage.** Applying more water than the crop and the soil can take, with no path for the surplus to leave, raises the water table into the root zone.

examTip.trap: Seepage from unlined canals is also a major cause and is sometimes offered; it is a particular case of too much water entering.
examTip.trick: Waterlogging is a balance problem: too much in, too little out.
examTip.mnemonic: Too much water, nowhere to go.

questions.stem: An anchor block on a penstock resists:
options: The weight of the pipe only
The unbalanced thrust at bends and changes of section
questions.solution: **The unbalanced thrust at bends and changes of section.** At every bend the change in momentum and pressure produces a resultant force that must be carried into the ground by a massive block.

examTip.trap: Expansion joints take the thermal movement, and saddles carry the weight between anchor blocks.
examTip.trick: A straight pipe needs no anchor; a bend does.

questions.stem: The per capita water demand for a town in Nepal is generally taken as:
questions.solution: **100-135 litres per head per day.** Urban design figures run around 100-135 lpcd including domestic, public and commercial demand; rural schemes use about 45 lpcd.

examTip.trap: 45 lpcd is the rural basic figure and is widely quoted in Nepali water supply practice.
examTip.trick: Urban demand is roughly three times the rural minimum.

questions.stem: The plasticity index of a soil is:
options: The plastic limit minus the shrinkage limit
The liquid limit minus the shrinkage limit
The liquid limit minus the plastic limit
The liquid limit divided by the plastic limit
questions.solution: **The liquid limit minus the plastic limit.** It is the range of water content over which the soil behaves plastically; a larger index means a more clayey soil.

examTip.trap: The shrinkage index is LL minus SL and the two indices differ by one limit.
examTip.trick: The plasticity index must be bounded by the two limits of plastic behaviour.
examTip.mnemonic: Plasticity index = liquid limit minus plastic limit.

questions.stem: The transition curve used between a straight and a circular curve on a highway is normally:
options: A circular arc of larger radius
questions.solution: **A spiral (clothoid).** The clothoid's radius decreases uniformly along its length, so the centrifugal force and the superelevation build up at a constant rate.

examTip.trap: A parabola is the standard *vertical* curve, and the two are frequently interchanged.
examTip.trick: Horizontal transition: spiral. Vertical: parabola.
examTip.mnemonic: Spiral in plan, parabola in profile.

questions.stem: Segregation in concrete means:
options: Separation of the coarse aggregate from the mortar
Rise of water to the surface
questions.solution: **Separation of the coarse aggregate from the mortar.** Dropping concrete from a height or over-vibrating it lets the heavy aggregate settle away from the paste, leaving a non-uniform mix.

examTip.trap: Water rising to the surface is *bleeding*, the other classic defect of a wet mix.
examTip.trick: Segregation separates solids; bleeding separates water.
examTip.mnemonic: Segregate the stones, bleed the water.

questions.stem: The performance bond required of a contractor in Nepali public procurement is usually:
questions.solution: **5% of the contract amount.** A performance security of about 5% of the contract price is furnished on award and released after satisfactory completion.

examTip.trap: The bid security is around 1-2% and the retention money about 5% of each payment — three different percentages in the same contract.
examTip.trick: Bid security small, performance security 5%.

questions.stem: A body floats in stable equilibrium when the metacentre lies:
questions.solution: **Above the centre of gravity.** With M above G a small tilt produces a righting couple; with M below G the couple overturns the body.

examTip.trap: Coincident M and G is neutral equilibrium — the boundary case, offered to see whether the inequality is remembered.
examTip.trick: The metacentre must be above the centre of gravity for the couple to restore.

questions.stem: The process of removing moisture from timber under controlled conditions is called:
questions.solution: **Seasoning.** Seasoning brings the moisture content down to equilibrium with the surroundings so the timber is dimensionally stable and resists decay.

examTip.trap: Preservation treats the timber against insects and fungus and is a separate operation that follows seasoning.
examTip.trick: Season for moisture, preserve against attack.
examTip.mnemonic: Season it dry, then preserve it.

questions.stem: The most efficient (most economical) trapezoidal channel section is one in which:
options: The depth equals the bed width
The hydraulic radius equals half the depth of flow
The hydraulic radius equals the depth
questions.solution: **The hydraulic radius equals half the depth of flow.** The section with the least wetted perimeter for a given area satisfies R = y/2, and a semicircle can be inscribed in it with its centre at the water surface.

examTip.trap: R = y is the condition approached by a very wide rectangular channel, which is a different limiting case.
examTip.trick: Best hydraulic section: half the depth, every time.
examTip.mnemonic: R = y/2 for the best section.

questions.stem: The capacity factor of a hydropower plant is the ratio of:
options: Average load to the maximum demand
Average load to the installed capacity
questions.solution: **Average load to the installed capacity.** It measures how fully the installed plant is used over the year; the load factor instead compares the average load with the peak demand.

examTip.trap: Load factor is the near neighbour and uses the maximum demand rather than the installed capacity.
examTip.trick: Capacity factor looks at the plant; load factor looks at the demand.
examTip.mnemonic: Capacity factor divides by what is installed.

questions.stem: The Nepal Engineering Council maintains a register of engineers in order to:
options: Ensure that only qualified persons practise engineering
questions.solution: **Ensure that only qualified persons practise engineering.** Registration is the mechanism by which the Council protects the public, since an unregistered person may not practise.

examTip.trap: Awarding degrees is the function of a university, and the Council recognises those degrees rather than granting them.
examTip.trick: A regulator licenses practitioners; it does not educate or employ them.

questions.stem: The penetration test on bitumen measures its:
options: Resistance to abrasion under the repeated passage of traffic
Hardness or consistency at a standard temperature
Specific gravity relative to that of water at the same temperature
Flash point, the temperature at which its vapour ignites momentarily
questions.solution: **Hardness or consistency at a standard temperature.** A standard needle under a 100 g load for 5 seconds at 25 °C penetrates the sample, and the depth in tenths of a millimetre is the penetration value.

examTip.trap: The ductility test measures how far the bitumen stretches before breaking, which is a different property from the same laboratory.
examTip.trick: A softer bitumen lets the needle in further, so a higher number means a softer grade.

questions.stem: A trickling filter treats sewage by:
options: Straining out the suspended solids mechanically through a fine medium
Precipitating the organic matter chemically with an added coagulant
Passing it over a bed of media on which a biological film grows
Forcing the sewage through a semi-permeable membrane under pressure
questions.solution: **Passing it over a bed of media on which a biological film grows.** Despite its name it does not filter: the micro-organisms in the film oxidise the organic matter as the sewage trickles past.

examTip.trap: The word "filter" makes mechanical straining the obvious reading, and it is exactly wrong.
examTip.trick: The treatment is biological; the media only provide a surface.

questions.stem: Differential settlement is more damaging than uniform settlement because it:
options: Induces additional stresses and distortion in the structure
Is always larger in magnitude than the total settlement of the building
Occurs far more quickly, leaving no time for the structure to adjust
Affects only the foundation and never reaches the superstructure above
questions.solution: **Induces additional stresses and distortion in the structure.** A building that settles evenly simply moves down; one that settles unevenly is forced out of shape, which cracks walls and overstresses members.

examTip.trap: Differential settlement is usually smaller in absolute terms than the total settlement, which makes "always larger" plainly wrong.
examTip.trick: It is the difference, not the amount, that damages.

questions.stem: In a load-bearing masonry wall, the slenderness ratio is the ratio of:
questions.solution: **Effective height to effective thickness.** It governs the permissible stress; a more slender wall carries less because it is more liable to buckle.

examTip.trap: Inverting the ratio would mean that thicker walls were more slender, which is the opposite of the meaning.
examTip.trick: Slenderness always puts the long dimension on top.

questions.stem: A hydraulic jump always occurs when the flow changes from:
questions.solution: **Supercritical to subcritical.** A fast shallow stream cannot slow down gradually; it rises abruptly, dissipating energy in the turbulence of the jump.

examTip.trap: The reverse transition happens smoothly, as at the brink of a fall, with no jump at all.
examTip.trick: A jump always goes from fast to slow, never the other way.
examTip.mnemonic: Super to sub, with a jump.

questions.stem: The soundness of cement is tested using:
questions.solution: **Le Chatelier apparatus.** The Le Chatelier mould measures the expansion caused by free lime; the limit is 10 mm for ordinary Portland cement.

examTip.trap: The Vicat apparatus performs the consistency and setting time tests on the same material in the same laboratory.
examTip.trick: Le Chatelier measures expansion, Vicat measures penetration.
